name: Nickels (Three Thirteen)
description: Nickels (also known as Three Thirteen or 65) is a progressive Rummy-style card game played over 11 distinct rounds. The game starts with three cards dealt to each player and ends with thirteen cards in the final round. It is known for its shifting 'Wild Card' rule, where the rank corresponding to the number of cards dealt becomes wild for that specific round. It is a game of patience, set-building, and risk-management, where the goal is to have the lowest cumulative score.

history.origins: Part of the larger Rummy family that includes Continental and Oklahoma Rummy. It gained popularity as 'Three Thirteen' in the early 20th century.
timeline: 1920s: Rules for 'Three Thirteen' are first documented in card game manuals.
1950s: Becomes a popular family camping game in North America.
1980s: Variations using multiple decks to support up to 10 players emerge.
Present: Commonly played as a 'Nickels' betting game where players put a nickel in the pot for each penalty point.
history.cultural: Often associated with social gatherings where it serves as a 'lengthy' game that allows for conversation while playing.
history.evolution: The game's progression from 3 to 13 cards mirrors the increasing complexity of set-building over the course of an hour.

setup.dealing: Round 1: 3 cards each. Round 2: 4 cards... Round 11: 13 cards each.

rules.objective: Have the lowest total penalty points at the end of 11 rounds.
rules.gameplay:
1. Draw a card (from deck or discard).
2. Form melds: Sets (3+ of a rank) or Runs (3+ of a suit in sequence).
3. Discard one card to end the turn.
4. **Going Out**: When a player can meld ALL their cards (using a final discard), everyone else has one last turn to improve their hand before scoring.
keyRules: Progressive rounds: 3 to 13 cards per round
Form Sets (3+ same rank) or Runs (3+ same suit in sequence)
Wild cards change each round (rank equals card count)
Draw from deck or discard, then discard one card to end turn
Going out: meld all cards; others get one last turn

strategy.basic: Prioritize your Wild cards. Since they change every round, never get too attached to a specific rank. A '3' is a treasure in Round 1 but just an annoyance in Round 2. Use your Wilds to bridge gaps in Runs (e.g., 4-Wild-6).
strategy.intermediate: The 'Last Turn' Warning: When an opponent goes out, you only have one move left. If you have high-value cards (Aces, Kings, Wilds) that aren't melded, discard them IMMEDIATELY. It is better to have an incomplete run of 3s than a loose King.
strategy.advanced: Discard Pile Psychology: Don't pick up a card from the discard pile unless it NATURALLY completes a meld. Picking up a discard tells your opponents exactly what suit or rank you are building, allowing them to 'block' you by holding the remaining cards of that set.
tips: In the final round (13 cards), players often 'go out' very quickly because the high number of cards increases the statistical probability of a natural run.
Aces can be low (A-2-3) or high (Q-K-A), making them versatile for long runs.

scoring.description: Numbered cards (2-9) = 5 pts; 10, J, Q, K = 10 pts; Aces = 15 pts; Jokers/Wilds = 25 pts.
scoring.winCondition: Have the lowest total penalty points at the end of 11 rounds.
